answer: Fog rolls in from the sea in a strict order, first the beach, then the inlet, then the higher ground, and claimants report the minute visibility drops at their step of that ladder. A beacon on the jetty flashes through the murk while quartz sand below stays invisible, so anyone reporting an early time from a high perch contradicts the sequence. A farm cannot fake the ladder because a single location yields only one rung, and inventing the rest means guessing minutes the fog had not yet reached.
